description: Bee is Amazon's wearable AI: a paid Frontier band or clip that listens through your day and turns conversations into searchable takeaways, summaries, to-dos, and drafted emails. GAIA is a proactive productivity OS that manages your email, calendar, tasks, and the rest of your tools autonomously, no wearable required.

faqs.answer: No. Bee listens through a paid wearable you wear on your wrist or clothing, with 7 days of battery. GAIA is pure software: it works with the phone and laptop you already own across web, desktop, mobile, and messaging apps.
faqs.question: Do I need Bee hardware to use GAIA?

faqs.answer: Bee turns conversations into searchable takeaways, summaries, suggested to-dos, and drafts of emails and calendar events, with mail, calendar, and Alexa integrations on its Pro tier. It captures and recalls. GAIA triages your inbox, drafts replies, schedules meetings, creates tasks, and runs multi-step workflows across your tools. Bee remembers the conversation; GAIA does the follow-up.
faqs.question: What can Bee actually do?

faqs.answer: Both remember, neither in the same way. Bee recalls what was said around you through its wearable. GAIA keeps graph-based memory linked to your tasks, emails, and events, then acts on it. If you want a record of conversations, Bee's wearable does that. If you want those conversations turned into completed work, that is GAIA.
faqs.question: Do Bee and GAIA both have memory?

faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA is source-available and runs entirely on your existing devices: the hosted plan is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month, and self-hosting via Docker is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs). Bee's Frontier is paid hardware, and Bee Pro, required for select features, is a paid tier with a trial period.

intro: Bee deserves credit for learning the lesson its predecessors missed: the Frontier costs less than a dinner out, runs for 7 days, and disappears onto your wrist or collar. It listens, and turns the day into searchable takeaways, summaries, suggested to-dos, and even drafted emails and calendar events. But capture is still the core loop. Nobody ever cleared their inbox by remembering it better. GAIA starts where Bee stops: it takes context and acts on it, triaging email, drafting the follow-up, creating the task, moving the meeting, across your tools, with no hardware at all. A wearable that remembers versus software that does.
